title: Investigate asymmetric input/output rates and streaming-floor mechanics for Hosted API enterprise offers
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Evaluate a split IO pricing model that bills input tokens and output tokens at different rates, combined with a small streaming minimum (floor) for low-volume streaming sessions, to improve margin on high-output workloads while preserving predictability for enterprise contracts.

Hypothesis: Charging asymmetric IO (higher output rate relative to input) plus a $0.10 streaming-floor per streaming session for sessions under a token threshold will increase hosted API gross margin by ~6–8% on customers with high output generation (summarization, codegen) while keeping churn under 1% for enterprise users with committed contracts.

Experiment design:
- Variant A (control): current unified per-token rate for IO and existing streaming behavior (no floor).
- Variant B (asymmetric IO): input tokens billed at baseline rate, output tokens billed at 1.25x baseline. No streaming-floor.
- Variant C (asymmetric IO + floor): same IO split as B plus a streaming-floor of $0.10 for streaming sessions that generate <200 output tokens.
- Sampling: random assignment across eligible hosted API accounts (excluding Dedicated and Private customers). Enterprise customers on active SOWs will be excluded from randomization but offered a separate pilot.

Measurement windows: 30-day rolling analysis with interim checks at 7 and 14 days. Primary metric: incremental gross margin delta (monetized). Secondary metrics: request volume, average latency, customer-reported billing disputes, and churn propensity signals (support tickets + account expansion holdbacks).
rollout_plan: Pilot for 4 weeks on 10% of eligible traffic for B and 10% for C. Monitor via billing pipeline and A/B dashboard. If margin uplift >5% with billing disputes <0.5% and no signal of increased latency or platform errors, expand to 30% traffic and prepare PR and pricing docs for enterprise pilots. Enterprise pilot will be opt-in and negotiated with legal to ensure SOW compatibility.
risks_and_mitigation: customer_confusion_about_io_split -> update billing docs and billing dashboard to show IO breakdown
legal_enterprise_sow_mismatch -> pre-clear with Legal and Sales Ops prior to outreach
unexpected_impact_on_latency_metrics_due_to instrumentation -> coordinate with Eng to gate rollout behind observability checks
